PE.name: Kiwicha
PE.citation: Peer-reviewed study (PMC10093863, 'Peruvian Amaranth (kiwicha) Accumulates Higher Levels of the Unsaturated Linoleic Acid'): confirms 'kiwicha' as the standard name for Peruvian Amaranthus caudatus, domesticated in Peru and found alongside Andean tombs over 4,000 years old. Widely used as the commercial/market name in Peru, not just a scientific-literature term.

BO.name: Kiwicha
BO.citation: Multiple Peruvian trade/agricultural sources (biocomerciokiwicha.blogspot.com, teofilocarranza.blogspot.com) document Aymara names for the species -'Kiwicha, Amaranto, Trigo Inca, Achis, Achita, Chaquilla, Sangorache, Borlas' - and its cultivation range as extending into Bolivia's high-altitude Aymara-speaking regions.

EC.name: Ataco
EC.citation: iNaturalist Ecuador species page (citing Wikipedia): Ecuador-specific common names listed are 'ataco, ataku morado, amaranto, bledo, quinua de Castilla'. The same source separately gives the Quechua name 'hawarcha' explicitly tagged '(Ecuador)', distinguishing it from the Peru/Bolivia Quechua form 'kiwicha'.

ES.name: Moco de pavo
ES.citation: Spanish Wikipedia article on Amaranthus caudatus, citing Colmeiro, Miguel: 'Diccionario de los diversos nombres vulgares de muchas plantas usuales o notables del antiguo y nuevo mundo', Madrid, 1871 - documents 'moco de pavo' as the name used in Spain.

GB.name: Love-lies-bleeding
GB.citation: Standard English ornamental-horticulture name specific to this species' distinctive drooping crimson tassel inflorescence, distinguishing it from grain-amaranth species (A. hypochondriacus, A. cruentus) sold under the generic name 'amaranth' - documented across UK gardening and horticultural trade sources.

US.name: Love-lies-bleeding
US.citation: Same standard English ornamental name as used in the UK, widely sold under this name in the US nursery/seed trade specifically for the ornamental tasseled form of A. caudatus.
